oewn-01655514-v.learner: To get something ready or put it in place so that it can be used or can start working.
examples: He laid the fire in the evening so it would be ready to light in the morning.

oewn-01547861-v.learner: To produce eggs from the body.
examples: The old hen still lays an egg almost every day.

oewn-13363150-n.learner: One of the equal parts into which a company's owned money is divided, where an official paper shows who owns each part.
examples: She bought a hundred shares in the railway company.

oewn-03974120-n.learner: A sharp steel wedge that cuts through and loosens the top layer of soil.
examples: The farmer sharpened the share of his plough before working the field.

oewn-02883550-n.learner: Ribbons tied or woven together to make a decoration.
examples: She wore a large red bow in her hair.

oewn-02883250-n.learner: The front part of a ship, boat or aircraft.
examples: Waves broke over the bow of the ship.

oewn-02882759-n.learner: A slightly bent piece of springy wood with tight strands of horsehair, used to play some string instruments.
examples: He tightened the hair on his bow before picking up the violin.

oewn-13918793-n.learner: Anything that has a curved shape.
examples: The branches met overhead in a bow above the path.

oewn-07244001-n.learner: A time when performers come back in front of the audience at the end of a play or concert to accept the clapping.
examples: After the last song the band came back on stage for another bow while the crowd cheered.

oewn-00548802-n.learner: One movement across the strings of an instrument with a bow, the curved stick with tight horsehair used to play it.
examples: Play all four notes in a single bow.

oewn-01182690-n.learner: Deliberately disobeying, or showing no respect for, the authority of a court or a law-making body.
examples: The witness who refused to answer was fined for contempt of court.

oewn-03629976-n.learner: A chess piece shaped like a horse's head, which moves two squares across and one up or down, or two up or down and one across.
examples: He moved his horse to protect the queen.

oewn-03543217-n.learner: A padded piece of gym equipment that stands on legs.
examples: She ran, jumped and swung her legs over the horse.

oewn-00752176-s.learner: So difficult that it is impressive.
examples: Finishing the whole house by Friday is a tall order.
He was fond of tall talk about honour and glory.

connotation.why: can mark a style as puffed up, against plain 'elevated'

oewn-07572730-n.learner: A food that people think of as especially fine to eat.
examples: Oysters were served at the dinner as a great delicacy.

oewn-05048657-n.learner: The state of not being physically strong.
examples: Because of the boy's delicacy, he was kept indoors all winter.

oewn-05114516-n.learner: The quality of being slim and thin.
examples: The thread was so fine that its delicacy made it almost invisible.

oewn-04640223-n.learner: A light quality in the way someone moves or behaves.
examples: She crossed the room with the delicacy of a dancer.

oewn-01195043-v.learner: To get some good or advantage out of something.
examples: Members enjoy special privileges, such as free entry.

oewn-02115276-v.learner: To have something that is good for you or works in your favour.
examples: She has always enjoyed good health.

oewn-05726503-n.learner: Any sounds that are pleasing and go well together.
examples: We fell asleep to the music of the waves on the shore.

connotation.why: calls a sound pleasing, against plain 'sound'

oewn-01165019-n.learner: The punishment you get for what you have done.
examples: He knew he would have to face the music when his father got home.

oewn-00141437-r.learner: In the way nature does it, by natural means, without help from anything made by people.
examples: The water in the pool is naturally warmed by hot springs below.
